title: A Moray Eel Has a Second Set of Jaws Hidden in Its Throat

scenes.text: A moray eel bites you twice. The second bite comes from its throat.
Most fish suck prey in by flaring their heads. A moray lives in cracks too tight for that.
So it grew a second set of jaws deep in its throat, with backward-pointing teeth.
When the front jaws clamp down, the throat jaws shoot forward, hook the prey, and drag it back.
It happens in a fraction of a second. X-ray video at UC Davis caught it in 2007.
The monster in Alien had the same trick. Nature got there first.

description:
A moray eel bites twice, and the second bite comes from a set of jaws hidden in its throat.
Most fish suck prey in by expanding their heads, but morays live in crevices too tight for that. Instead, a second set of jaws with backward-pointing teeth launches forward from the throat, hooks the prey and drags it back, all in a fraction of a second. UC Davis researchers caught it on X-ray video and published it in Nature in 2007.
Which sea creature would you least like to be bitten by?
subject: moray eel
first_comment: The throat jaws travel almost the full length of the skull to reach the prey. What other animal looks like it was designed for a horror film?
